text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — i'm worried about the complexity of handling late-arriving credits across epoch splits. if we split by hour windows then reconcile, we get simpler query semantics but a lot of cross-window handoffs. thoughts?

alex: +1 on the concern. main tradeoff: strict epoch boundaries make fast queries easy (no cross-window joins) but force us to either buffer late events (higher latency) or create complicated rewrite logic.

kevin: one option is 'append-only ledger with tombstone markers' — events always write into ledger, reconciliation job publishes finalized snapshots per-epoch. late credits just append and mark prior rows superseded. pros: easy audit trail. cons: storage blowup + more expensive compaction.

maria: tombstones seem ok for auditability, but how do we avoid query correctness races for SLOs? we don't want product teams seeing transient undercounts.

sophie: pragmatic approach: expose two views — realtime (best-effort, low-latency, eventual accuracy) and finalized (accurate after epoch finalization). clients pick. also, add a short TTL for 'pending' credits so realtime gives a hint.

alex: agree on dual-view. also propose a small opcode in the ingest path: "credit_state": ["pending","final"]. pending events are eligible for quick aggregation but excluded from billing until final. we can surface a "pending_delta" metric in console.

kevin: about reconciliation algorithm: consider prioritized replays instead of full compactions. only replay shards with >X variance or >Y late events. keeps compute costs down. pseudocode idea: 

```
for epoch in epochs_to_finalize:
  shards = find_shards_with_late_events(epoch)
  for s in shards:
    replay(shard=s, epoch=epoch)
    emit(finalized_snapshot(epoch,s))
```

maria: nice. two other constraints: 1) tenant isolation (no cross-tenant joins), 2) cryptographic fingerprinting for audit (so we can prove event lineage during disputes).

alex: fingerprinting is cheap if we compute a small digest (sha256 of event key + offset) at ingest. store digest in ledger row and in finalized snapshots. for tenant isolation, keep per-tenant shard namespace; replay only touches same tenant shards.

kevin: on idempotency: recommend a stable event id = sha256(request_id || ingestion_ts || tenant_id). reject duplicates at write-time with conditional put. reduces duplicate-credit risk during retries.

maria: good. last concern: how do we surface reconciliations and corrections to downstream billing pipelines without causing double charges?

sophie: emit correction events as negative credits with a link to the finalized snapshot digest. billing pipeline applies corrections idempotently by referencing snapshot digest. we also keep a 'correction window' policy: only auto-apply corrections within 30d, beyond that require manual review.

billing-bot: reminder: SLA for finalized accuracy is 24h. anything beyond needs engineering ops signoff. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: ok action items: (1) kevin + alex prototype append-only ledger + fingerprinting (2) sophie draft docs for realtime vs finalized views + pending_delta UX (3) i will write short runbook for correction-window policy. target: prototype v1 in 2 weeks. @kevin @alex @sophie please ack. :thumbsup:

alex: ack

kevin: ack

sophie: ack

maria: thanks everyone — i'll drop a follow-up RFC link here when v1 is up.
